text:
The 2024 [Robust Training paper](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) studies actual interaction deletion, especially removal of recent suffix items: [I₁,I₂] becomes [I₁]. Its training intervention is multiple-future-positive supervision, optionally combining BCE with a margin loss ordering future positives—not stochastic embedding corruption. More positives improve stability under deletion but can reduce clean next-item accuracy; the margin term addresses competition among positives. Controls include positive/negative counts and mixed-loss weights, rather than an input-corruption probability.

[S3-Rec’s implementation](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/CIKM2020-S3Rec/blob/master/datasets.py) replaces items with a dedicated learned mask token, preserving sequence slots and positional embeddings; masked slots remain attention-eligible during bidirectional pretraining. Its mask_p defaults to 0.2, with the final item always masked. Segment prediction masks a contiguous span rather than cropping the input. [CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2010.14395) constructs contrastive views using masking, cropping and reordering: mask fraction γ replaces items with a special [mask]; crop retains a contiguous fraction η; reorder shuffles a span fraction β. The paper’s “zero-masking” motivation does not establish a fixed-zero embedding implementation. Rates were tested from 0.1–0.9; excessive masking, aggressive cropping or excessive contrastive weight λ hurt accuracy. Mask-only SASRec augmentation also underperformed baseline on Sports.

Zeroing only item embeddings while retaining original positions and attention eligibility is therefore a distinct operator: positional signals remain and erased slots still participate in attention. It differs from deletion, learned-token masking and padding exclusion. These papers motivate studying it but do not directly establish its clean-accuracy benefit or novelty; tune its corruption probability and clean/corrupted training balance against the unchanged validation benchmark.
